description: Fifth eval set (v5) for the knowledge VS Code extension: 14 blast-radius engineering tasks that are provably cross-repository (every case requires >=3 repos) AND grep-resistant. Questions only — answers (expected file/repo sets), grep-resistance notes and cross-repo rationale have been stripped. Uses ONLY repositories present on disk (react, redux, redux-toolkit, react-redux, reselect, jotai, zustand, db, xyflow, query, table). knowledgeId = md5("owner/repo").
repoVersionsNote: branch and commit reflect the on-disk checkout at authoring time (verified via git). NOTE: react has moved since v3 (was 172742b, now f598ec1); all react paths in this file were re-verified at the new commit. [2026-08-02] Six repos re-pinned to the indexing layer's commits (react 3a717e42, redux-toolkit b1c51301, query 9d24c455, react-redux ad5d1e08, reselect 8d87c27b, redux 3aa561f9); all 14 cases' expected paths, key import couplings, and the query line-number citations (:132, :305) re-verified unchanged at the new commits.

cases.question: React tightens the rules for how a component may observe a data source that lives outside the renderer: the value read during render must now be referentially stable between render and commit, and the cleanup timing of the observation changes under concurrent re-renders. Every library in this folder that bridges its own state container into React components has such a bridge layer. Which files in which repositories implement that bridge and must change?

The optional 'is it still the same?' slot — the parameter that lets an application pass its own comparison function so a component skips re-rendering when the slice it derives from a store is equivalent but not identical — gets a new contract (the comparator must now also receive the previous selection as context). Which libraries in the folder expose or forward that slot to applications, and which files must change?

The dependency-injection mechanism by which a component locates the nearest state container placed above it in the component tree (instead of falling back to a module-level singleton) changes its propagation and default-value semantics under concurrent rendering. Which wrapper components and injection points across the folder are built on this mechanism and must be revisited?

The typed contract of the function an application calls to submit a state-transition event to the store — what shapes it accepts and what it hands back, including the extension that lets you submit a function (which receives the submitter and a state reader) instead of a plain event — is re-parameterized. Trace the full typing blast radius across the folder: the hook applications use to obtain the submitter, the async-task creator built on the extension, and the background-listener layer.

The store's interception pipeline — the triple-curried layer that wraps event submission so cross-cutting concerns (async work, logging, invariant checks) can run before and after each state transition — changes its curried signature and the capability object handed to each interceptor. Which repos in the folder define, implement, or assemble interceptors on this contract, and which files must change?

The definition of what counts as a legitimate state-transition event — a tagged plain object, plus the runtime guards that decide 'is this a plain object?' and 'is this a valid event?' — becomes stricter (e.g. prototype-chain rules change). Which repos re-export those guards, depend on them for invariant checking, or hand-roll a parallel implementation of the same event model that must stay consistent?

React tightens what a pending value that suspends rendering must look like: any awaitable consumed during render must carry a resolved status/value/reason protocol stamped on the object itself. Which async feeders across the folder produce, shim, or throw such pending values into the renderer, and which files must be updated?

The wire protocol for talking to the browser's time-travel debugging extension — the global the extension injects into the page, its connect/send handshake, and the store-enhancer type a connection must satisfy — changes. Which repos in the folder speak this protocol directly, and which files carry the protocol typing and the connection logic?

The re-entrancy contract for change notification is revised: what happens when an observer detaches itself, attaches a new observer, or triggers another state update while the notification sweep is still in progress. Several repos in the folder hand-roll their own notification loop with snapshot-the-observer-list semantics rather than sharing one implementation. Which files implement these loops and must be aligned to the new contract?

The caching contract for derived views changes: repeated reads with unchanged inputs must return the identical object reference so downstream consumers can bail out, and the cache-key strategy of the weak-reference-based cache is revised. Which repos implement or re-export this caching layer, which internal consumers sit on it, and which repo hand-rolls an equivalent cache for its derived-slice utility that must stay behaviorally consistent?

Across these libraries there's a recurring pattern: when the user's browser tab comes back to the foreground after being hidden, or when the device's network link is restored after dropping, any work that was deferred, paused, or has gone stale is automatically re-attempted or re-validated. Each library hand-wires the raw browser signals — the page-became-visible-again notification and the connectivity-came-back notification — into its own 'now is a good time to re-run' trigger, and each also decides whether an in-flight or held operation may resume based on whether the page is currently attended-to and the machine is currently reachable. Suppose we change that contract so a resume/revalidate trigger must carry a reason token describing which of the two conditions fired (regained attention vs. regained connectivity), and so that being in the foreground no longer gates resumption on its own. Find every file that subscribes to those browser conditions or gates resumption on them and would have to change.

Three of these libraries each independently roll their own policy for spacing out repeated attempts at an operation that keeps failing: the pause before the next try grows geometrically with the count of consecutive failures (roughly doubling each round), is clamped to a maximum ceiling so it never runs away, and after a bounded number of attempts the operation stops retrying and surfaces the failure. Some variants also fuzz the wait with a random component to avoid synchronized retries. Suppose we change this contract so the wait must be derived from wall-clock time elapsed since the first failure rather than from the attempt count, and so the ceiling becomes mandatory rather than optional. Find every self-contained implementation of the failed-attempt spacing/give-up policy that would have to be rewritten.

Across these libraries there is a recurring one-slot cache that guards an expensive derived computation: instead of hashing arguments, it holds onto the previous set of inputs as an ordered list and, on each call, walks that list position-by-position doing a reference check; only if the length differs or some slot points at a new object does it re-run the producer, otherwise it hands back the frozen prior output. Several of them also expose an opt-in instrumentation channel around this gate — one prints a color-coded elapsed-milliseconds badge tagged by a human-readable key only when a dev flag is on, another increments separately-resettable counters for how often the input list was re-gathered versus how often the producer actually fired, and a third emits a dev warning when the list changes size between renders. Suppose we change the shape of that ordered-input gate — say the element-wise reference test becomes a supplied comparator, or the instrumentation hook's signature changes. Which files implement this list-of-inputs recompute barrier and its timing/recount hook, and would all need to move together?

A convention shows up in all of these libraries: a writable piece of state whose write API accepts two interchangeable shapes — either a bare replacement value, or a callback that is handed the current value and returns the next one. At the write site each library does a runtime typeof-function fork: if it's a function it invokes it against the previous snapshot to derive the new value, otherwise it takes the argument as-is. Critically, the owner of that state may live outside the component that renders it — one library lets you hand ownership of the whole state bag to an external listener while still defaulting to internally-held state, and its React binding forwards the very same value-or-callback argument straight through into the framework's own setter so a caller can control just a subset. Another applies the same fork when you write into a keyed cache entry, running your callback against the previously-cached datum. If we tightened or widened the accepted shapes of this writer (e.g. added an async producer form, or passed a second argument to the callback), which files defining or applying this value-or-previous-callback convention would have to change in lockstep?
